note: CD20xCD3 bispecifics epcoritamab (approved 2023 on single-arm ORR) and mosunetuzumab, IgM imvotamab, toxin body MT-3724 and anti-CD20 mAb zuberitamab; models were monkey PD/toxicology, humanized-mouse xenografts and a QSP CRS model.
label: DLBCL (CD20-directed depleters)

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC); FDA BLA 761324 review confirms the 5-week cynomolgus study and pre-IND nonclinical package (2017).
engagement.note: Epcoritamab depleted B cells deeply and durably from monkey blood and lymphoid organs, equally after SC and IV dosing.
engagement.quote: In cynomolgus monkeys, DuoBody-CD3xCD20 demonstrated profound and long-lasting B-cell depletion from peripheral blood and lymphoid organs, which was comparable after subcutaneous and intravenous administration.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry; the monkey was the only cross-reactive toxicology species and the PD readout was peripheral B-cell depletion.

engagement.magnitude_basis: peripheral B-cell depletion, monkey vs patient (qualitative)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Registry NCT03625037 (first posted 2018-08-10) has no results posted. Population mixed B-NHL incl. DLBCL.
engagement.note: Patients' B cells were depleted as in monkeys, but CD20 depletion in patients was known from rituximab and mosunetuzumab before the 2020 monkey paper: retrodiction.
engagement.quote: Epcoritamab induced robust and sustained B-cell depletion, and CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell activation and expansion, with modest increases in cytokine levels.
engagement.judgement: Paired by me (Hutchings does not cite monkey data side by side). Depletion of the CD20-bearing cell read as proximal: it is the target cell itself, not occupancy. Patients were mixed B-NHL, DLBCL the largest group. Ruling 2026-11-09 (engagement retrodiction counts any drug with the same target and action): the monkey data were first public in January 2020, after rituximab and mosunetuzumab (ASH 2018/2019) had shown peripheral B-cell depletion in patients, so same -> retro.

dose.confidence_note: Applicant's position text in the FDA review; the EC20 numbers and derived starting dose are not given there.
dose.model: Human PBMC cytokine-release assay (EC20 starting dose)
dose.note: Mosunetuzumab's first-in-human starting dose came from EC20 values of cytokine release in human PBMCs; the values are not public.
dose.short: FIH start dose from PBMC EC20
dose.quote: The results (EC20 values) were used to inform the starting dose in the first in human study.
dose.reason: EC20 values and dose not public
dose.judgement: Kept untested: a starting-dose safety assay with its numbers withheld gives no checkable margin. Year set to the trial start (NCT02500407 first posted 2015-07-16) as a proxy for first use.

dose.model: Mechanistic QSP model of CD20xCD3 CRS (mosunetuzumab)
dose.note: Model built on monkey mosunetuzumab data predicted step-fractionated dosing would limit cytokine release without losing tumour response.
dose.short: Step-up dosing predicted to cut CRS
dose.quote: Simulations delineated mechanisms contributing to observed cell and cytokine (IL6) dynamics and predicted that initial step-fractionated dosing limits systemic T-cell activation and cytokine release without compromising tumor response.
dose.judgement: Opening entry. The regimen prediction (step-up allows higher doses tolerably) is the model's stated tolerability margin; it changed the ongoing Phase I schedule, so it is prospective.

dose.magnitude_basis: highest tolerated full dose step-up (60 mg) vs fixed (2.8 mg); grade>=3 CRS rate
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Registry NCT02500407 has no results posted. Aggressive B-NHL (mostly DLBCL) and indolent B-NHL pooled in safety. ASH 2019 abstract read in full on ashpublications.org.
dose.model: Mechanistic QSP model of CD20xCD3 CRS (mosunetuzumab)
dose.note: Step-up mosunetuzumab reached 60 mg with mostly low-grade CRS, as the model said; that result (ASH 2019) was public before the August 2020 model paper: retrodiction.
dose.short: Step-up margin already seen in patients
dose.quote: Cytokine release syndrome was mostly low-grade (grade ≥ 3: 1.0%) and mainly confined to cycle 1.
dose.reason: Retrodiction: drug's own step-up data public 2019
dose.judgement: Scored dose same with margin_stated: the model's tolerability claim for step-fractionated dosing held and full doses were reached. Whether the dose worked (aNHL ORR 34.9%) is efficacy, not scored here. Paired by me. Ruling 2026-11-09 (dose retrodiction counts only the same drug's own earlier patient result): Schuster et al., Blood 2019;134(Suppl 1):6 (13 Nov 2019, doi:10.1182/blood-2019-123742) reported step-up dosing up to 1/2/60 mg with CRS 28.4%, grade 3 1.4%, before Hosseini 2020 (28 Aug 2020). Same -> retro; year 2021 -> 2020, when the model side became public.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; PDX dose detail from FDA BLA 761324 review Table 5 (study GMB3013-083).
efficacy.model: Humanized-mouse lymphoma xenografts (CDX and DLBCL PDX)
efficacy.note: Epcoritamab shrank lymphoma cell-line xenografts in PBMC- or CD34-humanized mice; the one DLBCL PDX responded only at 5 mg/kg.
efficacy.quote: DuoBody-CD3xCD20 showed promising anti-tumour activity in vivo, also in the presence of excess levels of a CD20 Ab that competes for binding.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry. Most xenografts were Burkitt or mantle-cell lines; only one DLBCL PDX. Study year 2018 is a proxy from the BLA study numbering.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: tumour regression in mice vs objective response in patients
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. NCT03625037 has no registry results posted. Single-arm trial; FDA accelerated approval 2023 on this endpoint.
efficacy.model: Humanized-mouse lymphoma xenografts (CDX and DLBCL PDX)
efficacy.note: Single-arm EPCORE NHL-1 met ORR 63.1% (CR 38.9%); scored on its primary endpoint. DLBCL responses to CD20 depleters predated the 2020 xenograft paper: retrodiction.
efficacy.short: ORR met; anti-CD20 activity already known
efficacy.quote: At a median follow-up of 10.7 months, the overall response rate was 63.1% (95% CI, 55.0 to 70.6) and the complete response rate was 38.9% (95% CI, 31.2 to 46.9).
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me. The xenografts predicted antitumour activity, which the primary ORR endpoint showed. Hutchings 2021 already reported DLBCL ORR 68% but its primary endpoint was MTD. Design: single-arm, primary endpoint ORR by IRC, scored as a response where the model predicted one. Ruling 2026-11-09 (efficacy retrodiction counts any drug with the same target and action): rituximab monotherapy responses in DLBCL and mosunetuzumab aggressive-NHL ORR 34.7% (ASH 2019) were public before Engelberts 2020 (January 2020), so same -> retro.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: tumour regression in mice vs response/OS in patients
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry results read via the ClinicalTrials.gov API (primary outcome OS only; stratified HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.77-1.20, p=0.7285). The quote joins verbatim registry field values with ellipses; the registry has no prose sentence. Press release quote kept in patient_trials. No peer-reviewed paper found. Strengthens: adds the randomized phase 3 outcome trial (OS negative, outcome_tested) to the single-arm response retrodiction; status unchanged.
efficacy.model: Humanized-mouse lymphoma xenografts (CDX and DLBCL PDX)
efficacy.note: Phase 3 EPCORE DLBCL-1 vs chemoimmunotherapy missed its sole primary endpoint, OS (HR 0.96); PFS favoured epcoritamab. Status follows the retrodicted tumour-shrinkage surrogate.
efficacy.short: Phase 3 missed OS; surrogate already known
efficacy.quote: Overall Survival (OS) ... Stratified hazard ratio 0.96 ... 0.77 to 1.20 ... Stratified log-rank test ... 0.7285
efficacy.reason: OS missed; track stays on retro surrogate

patient_trials.quote: The study did not demonstrate a statistically significant improvement in overall survival (OS) (HR: 0.96 [95% CI 0.77 to 1.20]).

efficacy.judgement: The xenografts predicted tumour regression versus vehicle, a surrogate; the phase 3 is an outcome trial against active therapy, so outcome_tested negative and the status follows the surrogate, which on this track is a retrodiction (efficacy 2), hence retro, not same. Rule 2: the registry results record (tier 3, posted 2026-11-03) sets the status; the January 2026 press release is the earliest public date, so year stays 2026. OS is the only registered primary endpoint; the EHA 2026 PFS gain is a secondary result.

efficacy.note: Epcoritamab lysed primary DLBCL tumour cells from lymph-node biopsies (median 65%), including from patients relapsed or refractory to anti-CD20 therapy.
efficacy.short: Kills primary DLBCL cells ex vivo
efficacy.quote: In the presence of T-cells from a healthy donor, epcoritamab demonstrated potent activity against primary tumor cells, irrespective of prior treatments, including CD20 mAbs.
efficacy.confidence_note: Quote verbatim in the abstract (PMID 33602901); full text read on PMC7892878.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at publication; a system distinct from the draft's humanized-mouse xenografts (patients' own tumour cells, healthy-donor or autologous T cells, no animal). retrodiction flag is carried on the scored entry only.
efficacy.model: Ex vivo cytotoxicity against primary lymph-node B-NHL tumour cells (epcoritamab)

efficacy.note: The authors set the ex vivo killing beside the ongoing first-in-human trial's early responses in R/R DLBCL, which were already public when the work was published.
efficacy.short: Ex vivo killing matches known responses
efficacy.quote: These data support the single-agent activity of epcoritamab demonstrated in the ongoing first in human trial
efficacy.reason: Run after trial responses were known
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text (PMC7892878) cites the phase I/II trial's preliminary DLBCL/FL efficacy (ref 14, NCT03625037) as already reported; not found in BLA 761324 review.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction: the paper cites the trial's encouraging DLBCL responses, so the clinic knew the answer first; it reproduced activity, hence retro, not same. comparison_stated true because the paper itself sets model and trial side by side.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: ex vivo lysis of primary DLBCL cells vs objective responses in R/R DLBCL
efficacy.model: Ex vivo cytotoxicity against primary lymph-node B-NHL tumour cells (epcoritamab)

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; mortality and first-dose pattern from FDA BLA 761324 review (pharmacology/toxicology section).
safety.note: Monkeys showed first-dose cytokine release with clinical signs and one death at 1 mg/kg IV; SC dosing lowered peak cytokines.
safety.quote: Peak plasma levels of DuoBody-CD3xCD20 were lower and delayed after subcutaneous administration, which was associated with a reduction in plasma cytokine levels compared to intravenous administration, while bioavailability was comparable.
safety.judgement: Cytokine release is a CD3-engager platform harm, so the entry carries modality antibody. Monkeys can show cytokine release, so the prediction is admissible.

safety.magnitude_basis: occurrence and attenuation of cytokine release, monkey vs patient CRS grade
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Quote is a fragment of a longer abstract sentence (lowercase start). Later LBCL expansion (Thieblemont 2023) had grade 3 CRS 2.5% and ICANS 6.4% with one death.
safety.note: Subcutaneous step-up epcoritamab caused CRS in 59% of patients, all grade 1-2, as monkeys predicted; first public at ASCO 2020.
safety.short: CRS frequent but low-grade with SC
safety.quote: common adverse events were pyrexia (47 patients [69%]), primarily associated with cytokine release syndrome (CRS; 40 [59%], all grade 1-2), and injection site reactions (32 [47%]; 31 grade 1).
safety.reason: CRS present but mild, as predicted
safety.judgement: Paired by me. The monkey predicted cytokine release that SC dosing attenuates; patients had frequent but low-grade CRS. ICANS was not flagged as such in monkeys, though uncoordinated movements were noted, so I did not score a silence miss. Rule 6 (earliest date): the same CRS result (59%, all grade 1/2) was first public in the ASCO 2020 abstract (J Clin Oncol 38:2020 suppl, abstr 8009, May 2020), after Engelberts (23 January 2020), so year 2021 -> 2020 and still prospective.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. No published nonclinical safety study of MT-3724 found; the toxicology species is not confirmed. model_first_use_year 2014 is a proxy: the first-in-human trial NCT02361346 opened in 2014-2015, so toxicology preceded it.
safety.note: MT-3724 (Shiga-like toxin fusion) caused grade 2 capillary leak syndrome at 75 µg/kg; its monkey toxicology is not public.
safety.short: Capillary leak in patients; tox unpublished
safety.quote: Two patients (75 μg/kg/dose) experienced grade 2 treatment-related capillary leak syndrome.
safety.judgement: Capillary leak is a toxin-platform harm, so modality protein. Without a public toxicology source the prediction cannot be compared.
